correctness.rationale: From the five prime-power values of L2 one obtains exact exponent transition. W=a+b+c+2d+2e decreases by precisely 1 on each nonterminal step when a>0, otherwise 0. The proved invariant after a>=2 precludes all future idle steps. A positive initial 11 exponent forces a>=2 after one step; if initially absent, positive 13 exponent forces a>=2 after two steps. Those one or two initial zero-a events give exactly the case formula. The strict inequality follows termwise from 7>3,5 and 49>11,13. Exact integer independent checks: 6480 tuples; independent exponent checks: 52488 tuples; nine large boundary cases. Finite tests are corroboration, not universal proof.

value.rationale: The family is the first closed odd prime-support class through 13 with a delayed fork 13 to 11 to 3^2, not an arbitrary numerical cutoff. The exact classification gives all first-passage times for infinitely many four-free exponent parameters and identifies a sharp two-step startup phenomenon beyond the prior serial-chain 7-smooth family. It resolves the strict case of Defant's open bound throughout that infinite natural family. This is a complete structural classification, not an unrelated small computation or renaming.
